channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: The Solana Foundation takes a majority stake in CoinGecko, a popular crypto price-tracking platform with 18M registered users (Francisco Rodrigues/CoinDesk)
item.description: The Solana Foundation has secured a majority stake in CoinGecko, a major cryptocurrency data tracking platform with 18 million registered users. This strategic acquisition aims to vertically integrate market data infrastructure to bolster Solana's influence within the DeFi ecosystem's information gateway.

item.title: Microsoft makes Word, Excel, and PowerPoint generally available inside Copilot, which CEO Satya Nadella calls "the new OS for work" (Nick Indge/Ars Technica)
item.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint within Copilot at Ignite, shifting traditional software apps into secondary plugin components for AI Agents. The launch also introduces Copilot Autopilot, an autonomous agent for cross-service task delegation, powered by the new Work IQ organizational intelligence platform.

item.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
item.description: A study by Gallup and the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children's Hospital surveyed 15,925 youth across 16 countries, finding 33% of Gen Z rely on AI for companionship, peaking at 50% among daily users. While AI fills social gaps, it fails to match the emotional support of in-person bonds, with reliance on digital-only connections correlating with increased loneliness.

item.title: YouTube found a new way to inflate view counts
item.description: YouTube has introduced 'co-viewing' metrics for TV-based content, including long-form, Shorts, and live streams, by using a privacy-safe statistical model to estimate multiple viewers per device. This move aligns the platform with traditional TV industry standards, relies on demographic data rather than hardware sensors, and does not impact creator monetization.

item.title: LanceDB, which makes a multimodal lakehouse for AI training, built on the open format Lance, raised a $57.5M Series B led by Bessemer and Innovation Endeavors (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
item.description: LanceDB has secured $57.5 million in Series B funding, led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors, bringing its total capital to $98.5 million. Built on the open-source Lance format, the company provides a multimodal data lakehouse that unifies structured and unstructured data, addressing infrastructure bottlenecks in AI training workflows.

item.title: Sources: former Nvidia exec Jay Puri, who oversaw chip clients like Alice Huang, controlled chip sales to Super Micro; Puri is married to an ex-Super Micro exec (The Information)
item.description: Muddy Waters has initiated a short position on NVIDIA, alleging undisclosed personal ties between former EVP Ajay K. Puri and former Super Micro Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen. The move raises concerns over potential insider influence in GPU allocation, adding complexity to NVIDIA's current regulatory turmoil, including Congressional investigations into Chinese export control compliance.

item.title: Marco Rubio says there's "zero evidence" linking the recent FAA ground stop, Microsoft outage, and bank service issues, and the US isn't "under systemic attack" (Kiki Intarasuwan/CBS News)
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a press conference in the Philippines that recent technical outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and major banks are isolated incidents. Rubio emphasized that intelligence assessments show no evidence of malicious cyber activity, foreign state involvement, or a systemic attack on U.S. infrastructure.

item.title: Sources: a faction of Nvidia board members is pushing for Jensen Huang's return despite Chair Harvey Jones stating the board has no plans to reinstate Huang (Semafor)
item.description: A faction within Nvidia’s board is actively pushing for the return of former CEO Jensen Huang despite Chairman Harvey Jones' public denial of any such plans. Meanwhile, the board is concurrently vetting candidates for the CEO vacancy, including ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy, amid growing internal governance friction.

item.title: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial
item.description: US federal prosecutors accused Huawei of a 20-year scheme to defraud financial institutions regarding its Iran operations and conspiring to steal trade secrets from five American tech firms, characterizing it as a criminal enterprise. Huawei's defense lawyer, Brian Heberlig, countered in closing arguments that the prosecution failed to prove its charges, asserting that the banks were aware of the risks and that Huawei's market success was earned through innovation rather than illicit activities.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco
item.description: Investor Michael Burry, analyzing Anthropic's S-1 filing, identified $537 billion in compute procurement commitments to hyperscalers like Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, representing 12 times its annual run-rate revenue. Burry warned that these complex financing loops, involving vendor financing and structured credit, create systemic fragility, suggesting that any deceleration in AI demand could trigger catastrophic debt defaults across the ecosystem.

item.title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages
item.description: Wall Street executives and the NSA confirmed to Congress that recent nationwide tech outages were not cyberattacks, but resulted from legacy systems being overwhelmed by emergency patches triggered by AI-identified vulnerabilities. This highlights the fragility of aging IT infrastructure when subjected to the high-frequency deployment demands of automated security remediation.

item.title: Tech Paranoia Intensifies After Outages Roil Public Trust
item.description: Recent high-profile system outages across the NSA, FAA, and Microsoft have paralyzed essential services, fueling public anxiety despite no evidence of malicious cyber-attacks. Senator Mark Warner emphasized that AI-driven vulnerability discovery is forcing organizations to push updates at an unsustainable pace, exposing the systemic fragility of aging digital infrastructure.

item.title: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop
item.description: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation and operation of Juniper Networks routers, following findings that a recently installed unit in El Dorado, Arkansas, contributed to last week's nationwide air traffic control ground stop. Despite Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) asserting no defects, the incident, coupled with recent outages at the National Security Agency's classified communications network, highlights mounting concerns over the resilience of critical infrastructure supply chains and maintenance protocols.

item.title: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
item.description: Nvidia acting CEO Colette Kress confirmed the cessation of H200 AI accelerator shipments to China, ending a previous arrangement that allowed such exports under a 25% tariff regime. This decision follows the departure of CEO Jensen Huang and coincides with Nvidia's establishment of a board-level committee for national security and export compliance, addressing new restrictions on remote compute access for Chinese customers via foreign data centers.

item.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
item.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated at a post-Ignite roundtable that AGI could fundamentally reshape political economy by collapsing human capital into token capital, challenging the traditional role of firms. He rejected assigning moral status to AI models and warned that a monopolistic AI entity could pose systemic risks to healthcare, financial services, and democratic governance.

item.title: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)
item.description: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress confirmed on an investor call that the company will remain 'disciplined and selective' in allocating capital to Neoclouds and other AI-centric customers. Following the resignation of Jensen Huang, the board reaffirmed its stance against his reinstatement, prioritizing leadership stability and strategic rigor in supply chain resource allocation.

item.title: Apple HomeView teardown: a step backward in repairability compared to recent iPads and HomePods, with heavily glued display, speakers, and logic board (Carsten Frauenheim/iFixit News)
item.description: iFixit's teardown of the Apple HomeView reveals a heavy reliance on structural adhesives for its display, speakers, and logic board, marking a regressive step in modular design. Despite recent improvements in repairability across iPad and HomePod lines, HomeView’s integration forces high-risk disassembly that frequently leads to component failure.

item.title: Inside Microsoft’s giant Outlook outage
item.description: Microsoft's Exchange Online service suffered a sev0-rated outage initiated by server failures in Switzerland, which triggered failover mechanisms that propagated the issue, leaving over 80% of Exchange servers unresponsive. The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.

item.title: Malicious code delivered through Optimizely hits visitors to hundreds of sites
item.description: The website optimization platform Optimizely suffered a compromise of its infrastructure, leading to the distribution of malicious JavaScript via its legitimate CDN to 178 client sites, including CNN, Zoom, and Salesforce. The injected code targeted visitor devices with cryptocurrency wallet hijacking, payment data theft, and the deployment of iOS exploits such as DarkSword.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones announced during an earnings call that Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 due to personal conduct inconsistent with company standards. The board has unanimously accepted the resignation and confirmed there are no plans to reinstate Huang as CEO.

item.title: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones stated in the quarterly earnings call that the board unanimously rejects former CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement request, as the internal investigation into his personal conduct and alleged links to Chinese intelligence assets continues. Despite Huang's public efforts to return and support from political figures, the board maintains his removal to mitigate escalating regulatory and compliance risks following his resignation on November 12th.

item.title: My Husband and His Chatbot
item.description: As generative AI's conversational capabilities advance, it is rapidly transitioning from a task assistant to an emotional companion, introducing risks of alienation in personal relationships. Clinicians and legal experts observe that AI, due to its infinite patience and vast knowledge, is increasingly used for marital advice and emotional catharsis, though it also triggers concerns regarding social withdrawal and dependency.

item.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
item.description: NVIDIA Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% year-over-year increase, with data center revenue contributing $107.6 billion. The report confirms the successful launch of the Vera Rubin architecture and adherence to the established product roadmap.

item.title: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue up 103% YoY to $115.8B, above $109.1B est., Data Center revenue up 110% to $107.6B, and net income up 105% to $65.3B (Nvidia Newsroom)
item.description: Nvidia reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% year-over-year increase, driven by $107.6 billion from its Data Center segment. The company increased its share repurchase authorization by $150 billion and confirmed that the Vera Rubin platform has entered mass production.

item.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

item.title: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.

item.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
item.description: Alexandr Wang, Chief AI Officer at Meta, recently posted an AI-generated video on Instagram featuring fictitious video calls between Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Although the clip is labeled as AI-generated per platform requirements, it has intensified concerns regarding how deepfake technology blurs the line between reality and fabrication, posing risks to public figure integrity.

item.title: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say
item.description: US advertising technology firm AppLovin is in discussions to acquire Criteo. Criteo has seen its stock price decline by over 50% in the last five years, with its current market capitalization hovering around $1 billion, making it a prime candidate for industry consolidation.

item.title: CFTC Orders Kalshi to Take Down Markets on Trump’s Speeches
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has issued a formal order to the prediction market platform Kalshi, requiring it to halt trading and remove markets tied to public speeches made by President Donald Trump. This move underscores the regulator's intensified scrutiny of prediction markets' compliance and potential volatility post-election.

item.title: Corporate-Card Startup Ramp Raising Funds at $70 Billion Valuation
item.description: Corporate spend management platform Ramp is in early-stage negotiations for a new funding round, aiming to raise over $1 billion with leadership from Coatue Management and Thrive Capital. If successful, the company's valuation is expected to exceed $70 billion, marking its third fundraising event in a single year.
